{\n\treq    Request\n\tn      int\n\tnodes  []*node.Node\n\tnet    *netlink.Network\n\tevents eventHeap\n\n\tcounter int64\n\n\tnow float64\n\n\t// per-node counters\n\tarrivals   []int // packet copies that showed up (incl. duplicates)\n\tduplicates []int // arrivals recognized as already delivered/buffered\n\tbackpress  []int // arrivals rejected because the buffer was full\n\tbuffered   []int // arrivals accepted into the buffer\n\treleased   []int // buffered messages released by a later arrival\n\n\t// senderSeq[node] is the next broadcast sequence number.\n\tsenderSeq []int\n\n\tregistry map[string]node.Message\n\n\tdeliveries []Delivery\n\ttrace      []TraceEvent\n\n\t// pending arrivals not yet processed at the cutoff.\n\tpendingArrivals int\n}\n\n// Result is the complete simulator output.\ntype Result struct {\n\tNow             float64\n\tNames           []string\n\tDeliveries      []Delivery\n\tTrace           []TraceEvent\n\tNodes           []NodeFinal\n\tPendingArrivals int\n\tStats           Stats\n\n\tDiagnostics Diagnostics\n}\n\n// Stats holds run-wide counters.\ntype Stats struct {\n\tBroadcasts       int `json:\"broadcasts\"`\n\tArrivals         int `json:\"arrivals\"`\n\tDeliveredNew     int `json:\"deliveredNew\"`\n\tDuplicates       int `json:\"duplicates\"`\n\tBufferedTotal    int `json:\"bufferedTotal\"`\n\tReleasedFromBuf  int `json:\"releasedFromBuffer\"`\n\tBackpressure     int `json:\"backpressure\"`\n\tForcedDropped    int `json:\"forcedDropped\"`\n\tNetworkDropped   int `json:\"networkDropped\"`\n\tInFlightAtCutoff int `json:\"inFlightAtCutoff\"`\n}\n\n// New constructs a simulator from a request.\nfunc New(req Request) *Sim {\n\tn := len(req.Names)\n\ts := &Sim{\n\t\treq:        req,\n\t\tn:          n,\n\t\tarrivals:   make([]int, n),\n\t\tduplicates: make([]int, n),\n\t\tbackpress:  make([]int, n),\n\t\tbuffered:   make([]int, n),\n\t\treleased:   make([]int, n),\n\t\tsenderSeq:  make([]int, n),\n\t\tregistry:   make(map[string]node.Message),\n\t}\n\n\tcaps := req.NodeBuffer\n\ts.nodes = make([]*node.Node, n)\n\tfor i, name := range req.Names {\n\t\tcap := req.BufferCap\n\t\tif caps != nil {\n\t\t\tif c, ok := caps[name]; ok {\n\t\t\t\tcap = c\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\ts.nodes[i] = node.New(i, n, cap, req.Names)\n\t}\n\n\ts.net = netlink.New(n, req.DefaultLink, req.Links, req.Seed)\n\tfor id, dsts := range req.DropIDs {\n\t\tif len(dsts) == 0 {\n\t\t\ts.net.ForceDrop(id, -1)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tfor _, d := range dsts {\n\t\t\t\ts.net.ForceDrop(id, d)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tfor id, perDst := range req.HoldIDs {\n\t\tfor dst, delays := range perDst {\n\t\t\tfor _, d := range delays {\n\t\t\t\ts.net.ForceHold(id, dst, d)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Schedule broadcasts; stable order by (time, sender) gives deterministic\n\t// insertion sequences even when two broadcasts share a timestamp.\n\tbc := make([]BroadcastSpec, len(req.Broadcasts))\n\tcopy(bc, req.Broadcasts)\n\tsort.SliceStable(bc, func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\tif bc[i].Time != bc[j].Time {\n\t\t\treturn bc[i].Time < bc[j].Time\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn bc[i].Sender < bc[j].Sender\n\t})\n\tfor _, b := range bc {\n\t\ts.push(&event{time: b.Time, kind: evBroadcast, sender: b.Sender, dst: -1})\n\t}\n\treturn s\n}\n\n// Run processes events until the heap drains or MaxTime is reached.\nfunc (s *Sim) Run() *Result {\n\tfor s.events.Len() > 0 {\n\t\te := heap.Pop(&s.events).(*event)\n\t\tif s.req.MaxTime > 0 && e.time > s.req.MaxTime {\n\t\t\t// This and every remaining event lie beyond the cutoff.\n\t\t\ts.pendingArrivals = s.events.Len() + 1\n\t\t\tif e.kind == evArrival {\n\t\t\t\ts.pendingArrivals = s.countPendingArrivals(e)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t\ts.now = e.time\n\t\tswitch e.kind {\n\t\tcase evBroadcast:\n\t\t\ts.processBroadcast(e)\n\t\tcase evArrival:\n\t\t\ts.processArrival(e)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn s.buildResult()\n}\n\nfunc (s *Sim) countPendingArrivals(first *event) int {\n\tcount := 0\n\tif first.kind == evArrival {\n\t\tcount++\n\t}\n\tfor _, e := range s.events {\n\t\tif e.kind == evArrival {\n\t\t\tcount++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn count\n}\n\nfunc (s *Sim) processBroadcast(e *event) {\n\tsender := e.sender\n\ts.senderSeq[sender]++\n\tseq := s.senderSeq[sender]\n\n\t// The broadcaster's clock at broadcast time is its current clock plus\n\t// its own increment: the message depends on everything delivered so far.\n\tclock := s.nodes[sender].Clock()\n\tclock[sender]++\n\n\tid := s.req.Names[sender] + itoa(seq)\n\tmsg := node.Message{\n\t\tID:     id,\n\t\tSender: sender,\n\t\tSeq:    seq,\n\t\tClock:  clock,\n\t\tBody:   e.body(),\n\t}\n\ts.registry[id] = msg\n\n\ts.trace = append(s.trace, TraceEvent{\n\t\tTime:  s.now,\n\t\tType:  \"broadcast\",\n\t\tNode:  s.req.Names[sender],\n\t\tMsgID: id,\n\t\tClock: s.clockMap(clock),\n\t})\n\n\t// Local delivery first, then fan out to every other node.\n\tres := s.nodes[sender].Receive(msg)\n\ts.recordDeliveries(sender, msg, res, s.now, true)\n\n\tfor dst := 0; dst < s.n; dst++ {\n\t\tif dst == sender {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tplan := s.net.Send(id, Links may drop, duplicate and reorder packets, driven by\n// a seeded RNG plus explicit forced rules for reproducible scenarios.\npackage netlink\n\nimport (\n\t\"math/rand\"\n)\n\n// Link are the per-(source,destination) link parameters. Delivered is populated\n// only when Newly is OutcomeDelivered; its first element is the message\n// passed into Receive and the rest are cascade releases from the buffer.\ntype ReceiveResult struct {\n\tNewly     Outcome\n\tDelivered []DeliveredMsg\n}","originalFile":"package node\n\n// Message is a causal-broadcast application message.\n//\n// ID is the globally unique \"sender-seq\" identifier (e.g. \"A1\" for the\n// first message broadcast by node A). Sender is the global node index and\n// Seq that sender's 1-based broadcast counter. Clock is the message's\n// vector-clock dependency annotation.\ntype Message struct {\n\tID     string\n\tSender int\n\tSeq    int\n\tClock  VC\n\tBody   string\n}\n\n// Buffered is a message held until its dependencies are satisfied.\ntype Buffered struct {\n\tMsg Message\n}\n\n// Outcome classifies what happened to one receive attempt.\ntype Outcome string\n\nconst (\n\t// OutcomeDelivered means the attempt delivered the message and\n\t// possibly released a cascade of previously buffered messages.\n\tOutcomeDelivered Outcome = \"delivered\"\n\t// OutcomeBuffered means the message was stored for later release.\n\tOutcomeBuffered Outcome = \"buffered\"\n\t// OutcomeDuplicate means the message was already delivered or buffered.\n\tOutcomeDuplicate Outcome = \"duplicate\"\n\t// OutcomeBackpressure means the buffer was full; nothing changed.\n\tOutcomeBackpressure Outcome = \"backpressure\"\n)\n\n// ReceiveResult is the result of one Receive call. Newly is the message\n// passed into Receive; Released additionally lists buffered messages\n// released by the resulting cascade (empty unless Newly was delivered).\ntype ReceiveResult struct {\n\tNewly    Outcome\n\tReleased []Message\n}\n\n// Node is one simulated process.\ntype Node struct {\n\tIndex int\n\tNames []string // shared index->name table, used for diagnostics\n\n\tclock     VC\n\tdelivered map[string]bool\n\tbuf       map[string]Buffered\n\tbufCap    int // <= 0 means unbounded\n\thighWater int\n}\n\n// New builds a node. bufCap <= 0 means an unbounded buffer.\nfunc New(index int, n int, bufCap int, names []string) *Node {\n\treturn &Node{\n\t\tIndex:     index,\n\t\tNames:     names,\n\t\tclock:     make(VC, n),\n\t\tdelivered: make(map[string]bool),\n\t\tbuf:       make(map[string]Buffered),\n\t\tbufCap:    bufCap,\n\t}\n}\n\n// Clock returns a copy of the current delivered vector clock.\nfunc (n *Node) Clock() VC { return n.clock.Clone() }\n\n// Delivered reports whether the message has already been delivered.\nfunc (n *Node) Delivered(id string) bool { return n.delivered[id] }\n\n// InBuffer reports whether the message is currently buffered.\nfunc (n *Node) InBuffer(id string) bool { _, ok := n.buf[id]; return ok }\n\n// BufferedCount is the current number of held messages.\nfunc (n *Node) BufferedCount() int { return len(n.buf) }\n\n// HighWater is the largest the buffer ever grew.\nfunc (n *Node) HighWater() int { return n.highWater }\n\n// BufferCap returns the configured capacity (0 = unbounded).\nfunc (n *Node) BufferCap() int { return n.bufCap }\n\n// Snapshot returns copies of the buffered messages, deterministically\n// ordered by (sender index, seq).\nfunc (n *Node) Snapshot() []Buffered {\n\tout := make([]Buffered, 0, len(n.buf))\n\tfor _, b := range n.buf {\n\t\tout = append(out, b)\n\t}\n\t// Simple insertion-style ordering; buffers are small in practice.\n\tfor i := 1; i < len(out); i++ {\n\t\tfor j := i; j > 0 && lessMsg(out[j].Msg, out[j-1].Msg); j-- {\n\t\t\tout[j], out[j-1] = out[j-1], out[j]\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc lessMsg(a, b Message) bool {\n\tif a.Sender != b.Sender {\n\t\treturn a.Sender < b.Sender\n\t}\n\treturn a.Seq < b.Seq\n}\n\n// MissingDepsFor reports the unsatisfied predecessors of a buffered message.\nfunc (n *Node) MissingDepsFor(id string) ([]Missing, bool) {\n\tb, ok := n.buf[id]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\treturn MissingDeps(n.clock, b.Msg.Clock, b.Msg.Sender), true\n}\n\n// Receive processes one network arrival. State never changes on\n// duplicate or backpressure outcomes, so a rejected retry is safe and\n// causal order is preserved.\nfunc (n *Node) Receive(m Message) ReceiveResult {\n\t// Duplicate suppression is checked first so that a re-sent copy of an\n\t// already-held message is never mistaken for a buffer overflow.\n\tif n.delivered[m.ID] || n.InBuffer(m.ID) {\n\t\treturn ReceiveResult{Newly: OutcomeDuplicate}\n\t}\n\tif !Deliverable(n.clock, m.Clock, m.Sender) {\n\t\tif n.bufCap > 0 && len(n.buf) >= n.bufCap {\n\t\t\treturn ReceiveResult{Newly: OutcomeBackpressure}\n\t\t}\n\t\tn.buf[m.ID] = Buffered{Msg: m}\n\t\tif len(n.buf) > n.highWater {\n\t\t\tn.highWater = len(n.buf)\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn ReceiveResult{Newly: OutcomeBuffered}\n\t}\n\tn.markDelivered(m)\n\treturn ReceiveResult{Newly: OutcomeDelivered, Released: n.drainBuffer()}\n}\n\n// drainBuffer repeatedly releases every currently deliverable buffered\n// message. Each delivery advances the clock, which may unlock further\n// messages, so the loop repeats until a pass releases nothing.\nfunc (n *Node) drainBuffer() []Message {\n\tvar released []Message\n\tfor {\n\t\tvar head Message\n\t\tfound := false\n\t\t// Deterministic release order: lowest (sender, seq) among the\n\t\t// currently deliverable candidates.\n\t\tfor _, b := range n.buf {\n\t\t\tif !Deliverable(n.clock, b.Msg.Clock, b.Msg.Sender) {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif !found || lessMsg(b.Msg, head) {\n\t\t\t\thead = b.Msg\n\t\t\t\tfound = true\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif !found {\n\t\t\treturn released\n\t\t}\n\t\tdelete(n.buf, head.ID)\n\t\tn.markDelivered(head)\n\t\treleased = append(released, head)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (n *Node) markDelivered(m Message) {\n\tn.delivered[m.ID] = true\n\tn.clock.Merge(m.Clock)\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":34,"oldLines":12,"newStart":34,"newLines":20,"lines":["   OutcomeBackpressure Outcome = \"backpressure\""," )"," ","-// ReceiveResult is the result of one Receive call. Sender is the global node index and\n// Seq that sender's 1-based broadcast counter. Clock is the message's\n// vector-clock dependency annotation.\ntype Message struct {\n\tID     string\n\tSender int\n\tSeq    int\n\tClock  VC\n\tBody   string\n}\n\n// Buffered is a message held until its dependencies are satisfied.\ntype Buffered struct {\n\tMsg Message\n}\n\n// Outcome classifies what happened to one receive attempt.\ntype Outcome string\n\nconst (\n\t// OutcomeDelivered means the attempt delivered the message and\n\t// possibly released a cascade of previously buffered messages.\n\tOutcomeDelivered Outcome = \"delivered\"\n\t// OutcomeBuffered means the message was stored for later release.\n\tOutcomeBuffered Outcome = \"buffered\"\n\t// OutcomeDuplicate means the message was already delivered or buffered.\n\tOutcomeDuplicate Outcome = \"duplicate\"\n\t// OutcomeBackpressure means the buffer was full; nothing changed.\n\tOutcomeBackpressure Outcome = \"backpressure\"\n)\n\n// DeliveredMsg pairs a delivered message with the receiver's clock as it\n// stood immediately after that delivery (head delivery plus each cascade\n// release has its own snapshot).\ntype DeliveredMsg struct {\n\tMsg        Message\n\tClockAfter VC\n}\n\n// ReceiveResult is the result of one Receive call. Delivered is populated\n// only when Newly is OutcomeDelivered; its first element is the message\n// passed into Receive and the rest are cascade releases from the buffer.\ntype ReceiveResult struct {\n\tNewly     Outcome\n\tDelivered []DeliveredMsg\n}\n\n// Node is one simulated process.\ntype Node struct {\n\tIndex int\n\tNames []string // shared index->name table, used for diagnostics\n\n\tclock     VC\n\tdelivered map[string]bool\n\tbuf       map[string]Buffered\n\tbufCap    int // <= 0 means unbounded\n\thighWater int\n}\n\n// New builds a node. bufCap <= 0 means an unbounded buffer.\nfunc New(index int, n int, bufCap int, names []string) *Node {\n\treturn &Node{\n\t\tIndex:     index,\n\t\tNames:     names,\n\t\tclock:     make(VC, n),\n\t\tdelivered: make(map[string]bool),\n\t\tbuf:       make(map[string]Buffered),\n\t\tbufCap:    bufCap,\n\t}\n}\n\n// Clock returns a copy of the current delivered vector clock.\nfunc (n *Node) Clock() VC { return n.clock.Clone() }\n\n// Delivered reports whether the message has already been delivered.\nfunc (n *Node) Delivered(id string) bool { return n.delivered[id] }\n\n// InBuffer reports whether the message is currently buffered.\nfunc (n *Node) InBuffer(id string) bool { _, ok := n.buf[id]; return ok }\n\n// BufferedCount is the current number of held messages.\nfunc (n *Node) BufferedCount() int { return len(n.buf) }\n\n// HighWater is the largest the buffer ever grew.\nfunc (n *Node) HighWater() int { return n.highWater }\n\n// BufferCap returns the configured capacity (0 = unbounded).\nfunc (n *Node) BufferCap() int { return n.bufCap }\n\n// Snapshot returns copies of the buffered messages, deterministically\n// ordered by (sender index, seq).\nfunc (n *Node) Snapshot() []Buffered {\n\tout := make([]Buffered, 0, len(n.buf))\n\tfor _, b := range n.buf {\n\t\tout = append(out, b)\n\t}\n\t// Simple insertion-style ordering; buffers are small in practice.\n\tfor i := 1; i < len(out); i++ {\n\t\tfor j := i; j > 0 && lessMsg(out[j].Msg, out[j-1].Msg); j-- {\n\t\t\tout[j], out[j-1] = out[j-1], out[j]\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc lessMsg(a, b Message) bool {\n\tif a.Sender != b.Sender {\n\t\treturn a.Sender < b.Sender\n\t}\n\treturn a.Seq < b.Seq\n}\n\n// MissingDepsFor reports the unsatisfied predecessors of a buffered message.\nfunc (n *Node) MissingDepsFor(id string) ([]Missing, bool) {\n\tb, ok := n.buf[id]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\treturn MissingDeps(n.clock, b.Msg.Clock, b.Msg.Sender), true\n}\n\n// Receive processes one network arrival. State never changes on\n// duplicate or backpressure outcomes, so a rejected retry is safe and\n// causal order is preserved.\nfunc (n *Node) Receive(m Message) ReceiveResult {\n\t// Duplicate suppression is checked first so that a re-sent copy of an\n\t// already-held message is never mistaken for a buffer overflow.\n\tif n.delivered[m.ID] || n.InBuffer(m.ID) {\n\t\treturn ReceiveResult{Newly: OutcomeDuplicate}\n\t}\n\tif !Deliverable(n.clock, m.Clock, m.Sender) {\n\t\tif n.bufCap > 0 && len(n.buf) >= n.bufCap {\n\t\t\treturn ReceiveResult{Newly: OutcomeBackpressure}\n\t\t}\n\t\tn.buf[m.ID] = Buffered{Msg: m}\n\t\tif len(n.buf) > n.highWater {\n\t\t\tn.highWater = len(n.buf)\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn ReceiveResult{Newly: OutcomeBuffered}\n\t}\n\tn.markDelivered(m)\n\treturn ReceiveResult{Newly: OutcomeDelivered, Released: n.drainBuffer()}\n}\n\n// drainBuffer repeatedly releases every currently deliverable buffered\n// message. Each delivery advances the clock, which may unlock further\n// messages, so the loop repeats until a pass releases nothing.\nfunc (n *Node) drainBuffer() []Message {\n\tvar released []Message\n\tfor {\n\t\tvar head Message\n\t\tfound := false\n\t\t// Deterministic release order: lowest (sender, seq) among the\n\t\t// currently deliverable candidates.\n\t\tfor _, b := range n.buf {\n\t\t\tif !Deliverable(n.clock, b.Msg.Clock, b.Msg.Sender) {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif !found || lessMsg(b.Msg, head) {\n\t\t\t\thead = b.Msg\n\t\t\t\tfound = true\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif !found {\n\t\t\treturn released\n\t\t}\n\t\tdelete(n.buf, head.ID)\n\t\tn.markDelivered(head)\n\t\treleased = append(released, head)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (n *Node) markDelivered(m Message) {\n\tn.delivered[m.ID] = true\n\tn.clock.Merge(m.Clock)\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":144,"oldLines":14,"newStart":144,"newLines":16,"lines":["     return ReceiveResult{Newly: OutcomeBuffered}","   }","   n.markDelivered(m)","-  return ReceiveResult{Newly: OutcomeDelivered, Released: n.drainBuffer()}","+  delivered := []DeliveredMsg{{Msg: m, ClockAfter: n.clock.Clone()}}","+  delivered = append(delivered, n.drainBuffer()...)","+  return ReceiveResult{Newly: OutcomeDelivered, Delivered: delivered}"," }"," "," // drainBuffer repeatedly releases every currently deliverable buffered"," // message. s.req.Names[sender],\n\t\t\t\tDst:    s.req.Names[dst],\n\t\t\t\tMsgID:  id,\n\t\t\t\tReason: \"forced\",\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\t// The plan struct can't distinguish forced vs random    s.now,\n\t\t\tType:        \"duplicate\",\n\t\t\tNode:        s.req.Names[dst],\n\t\t\tMsgID:       e.msg.ID,\n\t\t\tArrivedAt:   s.now,\n\t\t\tScheduledAt: e.scheduled,\n\t\t})\n\tcase s.req.Names[at]}\n\t}\n\t// Cross-node predecessor gaps.\n\tmiss := node.MissingDeps(nd.Clock(), m.Clock, m.Sender)\n\tsort.Slice(miss, func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\tif miss[i].From != miss[j].From {\n\t\t\treturn miss[i].From < miss[j].From\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn miss[i].Need < miss[j].Need\n\t})\n\troots = append(roots, m.ID+\"@\"+s.req.Names[at])\n\tchain = []string{m.ID}\n\tfor _, mm := range miss {\n\t\tpredID := s.req.Names[mm.From] + itoa(mm.Need)\n\t\troots = append(roots, predID+\"@\"+s.req.Names[at])\n\t\tchain = append(chain, predID)\n\t}\n\treturn chain, dedup(roots)\n}\n\nfunc dedup(in []string) []string {\n\tseen := map[string]bool{}\n\tout := in[:0]\n\tfor _, x := range in {\n\t\tif !seen[x] {\n\t\t\tseen[x] = true\n\t\t\tout = append(out, x)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// inFlight reports whether a packet copy for msgID is still queued towards\n// node at (the heap content is read directly; used only at cutoff).\nfunc (s *Sim) inFlight(at int, msgID string) bool {\n\tfor _, e := range s.events {\n\t\tif e.kind == evArrival && e.dst == at && e.msg.ID == msgID {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\nfunc (s *Sim) nameIndex(name string) int {\n\tfor i, n := range s.req.Names {\n\t\tif n == name {\n\t\t\treturn i\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn -1\n}\n\n// checkCausalOrder replays the recorded delivery log per node and verifies\n// every delivery actually satisfied the vector-clock rule. (The simulator\n// should never produce a violation; this independently re-checks it.)\nfunc (s *Sim) checkCausalOrder() []CausalViolation {\n\tclock := map[string][]int{}\n\tfor _, name := range s.req.Names {\n\t\tclock[name] = make([]int, s.n)\n\t}\n\tvar viols []CausalViolation\n\tfor _, d := range s.deliveries {\n\t\tsenderName := senderOf(d.MsgID, s.req.Names)\n\t\tsender := s.nameIndex(senderName)\n\t\tcur := clock[d.Node]\n\t\tmsg, ok := s.registry[d.MsgID]\n\t\tif !ok || sender < 0 {\n\t\t\tviols = append(viols, CausalViolation{Node: d.Node, MsgID: d.MsgID, Detail: \"unknown message\"})\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif !node.Deliverable(node.VC(cur), msg.Clock, sender) {\n\t\t\tviols = append(viols, CausalViolation{\n\t\t\t\tNode: d.Node, MsgID: d.MsgID,\n\t\t\t\tDetail: \"delivered while vector-clock dependencies were unsatisfied\",\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t\tnode.VC(cur).Merge(msg.Clock)\n\t}\n\treturn viols\n}\n\nfunc senderOf(msgID string, names []string) string {\n\t// IDs are \"<name><seq>\"; pick the longest name that is a prefix so\n\t// multi-character node names work.\n\tbest := \"\"\n\tfor _, n := range names {\n\t\tif len(msgID) > len(n) && msgID[:len(n)] == n && len(n) > len(best) {\n\t\t\tbest = n\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn best\n}\n\nfunc sortReports(r []MissingReport) {\n\tsort.Slice(r, func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\tif r[i].Node != r[j].Node {\n\t\t\treturn r[i].Node < r[j].Node\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn r[i].MsgID < r[j].MsgID\n\t})\n}\n\nfunc sortBlocked(r []BlockedReport) {\n\tsort.Slice(r, func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\tif r[i].Node != r[j].Node {\n\t\t\treturn r[i].Node < r[j].Node\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn r[i].MsgID < r[j].MsgID\n\t})\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"25b6177c-d36e-46e4-85ae-f6784145edbc","session_id":"17e0c499-e52d-4d51-ae66-30adfd094eb4","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp28/a","sessionId":"17e0c499-e52d-4d51-ae66-30adfd094eb4","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp28-a","slug":"twinkly-mixing-kettle"}

Dst omitted/empty means every node.\ntype DropEntry struct {\n\tMsgID string   `json:\"msgId\"`\n\tDst   []string `json:\"dst\"`\n}\n\n// HoldEntry forces extra delayed copies of MsgID.\n//\n// Delay may be a number (one extra copy arriving at that absolute delay)\n// or a list (several extra copies). Dst omitted means every node.\ntype HoldEntry struct {\n\tMsgID string    `json:\"msgId\"`\n\tDst   []string  `json:\"dst\"`\n\tDelay flexFloat `json:\"delay\"`\n}\n\n// BroadcastJSON schedules one broadcast.\ntype BroadcastJSON struct {\n\tTime   float64 `json:\"time\"`\n\tFrom   string  `json:\"from\"`\n\tBody   string  `json:\"body\"`\n}\n\n// flexFloat accepts either a single number or a list of numbers in JSON.\ntype flexFloat []float64\n\nfunc (f *flexFloat) UnmarshalJSON(b []byte) error {\n\tvar single float64\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(b, &single); err == nil {\n\t\t*f = []float64{single}\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tvar many []float64\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(b, &many); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"delay must be a number or an array of numbers\")\n\t}\n\t*f = many\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// DefaultBufferCap is used when bufferCap is omitted.\nconst DefaultBufferCap = 1024\n\n// Validate checks the request and fills defaults.\nfunc (r *Request) Validate() error {\n\tif len(r.Nodes) < 1 {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"nodes: at least one node is required\")\n\t}\n\tseen := map[string]bool{}\n\tfor _, n := range r.Nodes {\n\t\tif n == \"\" {\n\t\t\treturn r.Network.Default != nil {\n\t\tif err := r.Network.Default.validate(\"network.default\"); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tfor i, le := range r.Network.Links {\n\t\tif !seen[le.From] || {\n\t\tif d.MsgID == \"\" {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"network.dropIds[%d]: msgId is required\", i)\n\t\t}\n\t\tfor _, dst := range d.Dst {\n\t\t\tif !seen[dst] {\n\t\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"network.dropIds[%d]: unknown dst %q\", i, dst)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tfor i, h := range r.Network.HoldIDs {\n\t\tif h.MsgID == \"\" {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"network.holdIds[%d]: b.Time < 0 {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"broadcasts[%d]: time must be >= 0\", i)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (l *LinkJSON) validate(path string) error {\n\tcheck := func(v *float64, name The timing makes each broadcast\n// depend causally on the previous one, so out-of-order links force\n// buffering along the chain.\n//\n// If lossLast is true, the penultimate chain message is force-dropped at\n// the final node, so the final message is permanently blocked there and the\n// diagnostics report a root-cause chain.\nfunc Chain(n int, seed int64, lossLast bool) jsonio.Request {\n\tif n < 2 {\n\t\tn = 2\n\t}\n\tnames := nodeNames(n)\n\treq := jsonio.Request{\n\t\tNodes:     names,\n\t\tBufferCap: 1024,\n\t\tNetwork: jsonio.NetworkConfig{\n\t\t\tSeed: ptr(seed),\n\t\t\tDefault: &jsonio.LinkJSON{\n\t\t\t\tBaseDelay:  ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t\tJitter:     ptr(0.9),\n\t\t\t\tReorderJit: ptr(0.6),\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\treq.Broadcasts = append(req.Broadcasts, jsonio.BroadcastJSON{\n\t\t\tTime: float64(i) * 4.0,\n\t\t\tFrom: names[i%n],\n\t\t\tBody: fmt.Sprintf(\"chain-step-%d\", i+1),\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\tif lossLast && n >= 2 {\n\t\tpen := names[n-2]\n\t\tlast := names[n-1]\n\t\treq.Network.DropIDs = append(req.Network.DropIDs, jsonio.DropEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: pen + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDst:   []string{last},\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\treturn req\n}\n\n// Concurrent builds an independent-burst request: every node broadcasts\n// twice in a short window, messages carry no cross-node dependencies. With\n// jittered links they arrive out of order but must all deliver immediately\n// (no causal buffering between independent messages); duplicate copies are\n// suppressed.\nfunc Concurrent(n int, seed int64, duplicate bool) jsonio.Request {\n\tif n < 2 {\n\t\tn = 2\n\t}\n\tnames := nodeNames(n)\n\treq := jsonio.Request{\n\t\tNodes:     names,\n\t\tBufferCap: 1024,\n\t\tNetwork: jsonio.NetworkConfig{\n\t\t\tSeed: ptr(seed),\n\t\t\tDefault: &jsonio.LinkJSON{\n\t\t\t\tBaseDelay:  ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t\tJitter:     ptr(0.95),\n\t\t\t\tReorderJit: ptr(0.9),\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tt := 0.0\n\tfor r := 0; r < 2; r++ {\n\t\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\t\treq.Broadcasts = append(req.Broadcasts, jsonio.BroadcastJSON{\n\t\t\t\tTime: t,\n\t\t\t\tFrom: names[i],\n\t\t\t\tBody: fmt.Sprintf(\"round-%d-node-%s\", r+1, names[i]),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t\tt += 0.2\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif duplicate {\n\t\t// Force an extra late copy of the first broadcast to every node, so\n\t\t// duplicate suppression is always demonstrable regardless of RNG.\n\t\treq.Network.HoldIDs = append(req.Network.HoldIDs, jsonio.HoldEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: names[0] + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDelay: flex(20),\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\treturn req\n}\n\n// flex is a tiny helper to build the flex float list.\nfunc flex(x float64) []float64 { return []float64{x} }\n\nfunc nodeNames(n int) []string {\n\tout := make([]string, n)\n\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\tout[i] = string(rune('A' + i))\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc ptr[T any](v T) *T { return &v }\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"d6b3f0b7-59e3-4867-8706-4a7ca0b06b45","session_id":"17e0c499-e52d-4d51-ae66-30adfd094eb4","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp28/a","sessionId":"17e0c499-e52d-4d51-ae66-30adfd094eb4","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp28-a","slug":"twinkly-mixing-kettle"}

The timing makes each broadcast\n// depend causally on the previous one, so out-of-order links force\n// buffering along the chain.\n//\n// If lossLast is true, the penultimate chain message is force-dropped at\n// the final node, so the final message is permanently blocked there and the\n// diagnostics report a root-cause chain.\nfunc Chain(n int, seed int64, lossLast bool) jsonio.Request {\n\tif n < 2 {\n\t\tn = 2\n\t}\n\tnames := nodeNames(n)\n\treq := jsonio.Request{\n\t\tNodes:     names,\n\t\tBufferCap: 1024,\n\t\tNetwork: jsonio.NetworkConfig{\n\t\t\tSeed: ptr(seed),\n\t\t\tDefault: &jsonio.LinkJSON{\n\t\t\t\tBaseDelay:  ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t\tJitter:     ptr(0.9),\n\t\t\t\tReorderJit: ptr(0.6),\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\treq.Broadcasts = append(req.Broadcasts, jsonio.BroadcastJSON{\n\t\t\tTime: float64(i) * 4.0,\n\t\t\tFrom: names[i%n],\n\t\t\tBody: fmt.Sprintf(\"chain-step-%d\", i+1),\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\tif lossLast && n >= 2 {\n\t\tpen := names[n-2]\n\t\tlast := names[n-1]\n\t\treq.Network.DropIDs = append(req.Network.DropIDs, jsonio.DropEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: pen + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDst:   []string{last},\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\treturn req\n}\n\n// Concurrent builds an independent-burst request: every node broadcasts\n// twice in a short window, messages carry no cross-node dependencies. With\n// jittered links they arrive out of order but must all deliver immediately\n// (no causal buffering between independent messages); duplicate copies are\n// suppressed.\nfunc Concurrent(n int, seed int64, duplicate bool) jsonio.Request {\n\tif n < 2 {\n\t\tn = 2\n\t}\n\tnames := nodeNames(n)\n\treq := jsonio.Request{\n\t\tNodes:     names,\n\t\tBufferCap: 1024,\n\t\tNetwork: jsonio.NetworkConfig{\n\t\t\tSeed: ptr(seed),\n\t\t\tDefault: &jsonio.LinkJSON{\n\t\t\t\tBaseDelay:  ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t\tJitter:     ptr(0.95),\n\t\t\t\tReorderJit: ptr(0.9),\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tt := 0.0\n\tfor r := 0; {"parentUuid":"91faf4a7-18f5-4258-98dd-b0a9e2243e79","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_6pmemk6ahpr2tg9ulfbs775x","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp28/a/internal/node/node_test.go","content":"package node\n\nimport \"testing\"\n\nfunc vcOf(n int, pairs ...int) VC {\n\tv := make(VC, n)\n\tfor i := 0; i+1 < len(pairs); i += 2 {\n\t\tv[pairs[i]] = pairs[i+1]\n\t}\n\treturn v\n}\n\nfunc TestDeliverableRule(t *testing.T) {\n\t// cur = {A:1,B:0}; A2 requires exactly A=2 and nothing ahead.\n\tcur := vcOf(2, 0, 1)\n\tif !Deliverable(cur, vcOf(2, 0, 2), 0) {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"A2 should be deliverable after A1\")\n\t}\n\t// A3 is a same-stream gap.\n\tif Deliverable(cur, vcOf(2, 0, 3), 0) {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"A3 must not deliver before A2\")\n\t}\n\t// B1 depending on A=2 is a cross-node gap.\n\tif Deliverable(cur, vcOf(2, 0, 2, 1, 1), 1) {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"B1(A=2) must not deliver while A is at 1\")\n\t}\n\t// Independent B1 is fine.\n\tif !Deliverable(cur, vcOf(2, 0, 1, 1, 1), 1) {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"independent B1 should deliver\")\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestBufferReleaseCascade(t *testing.T) {\n\tnames := []string{\"A\", \"B\", \"C\"}\n\tn := New(2, 3, 10, names) // node C\n\n\ta1 := Message{ID: \"A1\", Sender: 0, Seq: 1, Clock: vcOf(3, 0, 1)}\n\tb1 := Message{ID: \"B1\", Sender: 1, Seq: 1, Clock: vcOf(3, 0, 1, 1, 1)}\n\tc1 := Message{ID: \"C1\", Sender: 2, Seq: 1, Clock: vcOf(3, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1)}\n\n\t// Out of order: C1 arrives first (needs A1 and B1), then B1 (needs A1),\n\t// then A1.\n\tif r := n.Receive(c1); r.Newly != OutcomeBuffered {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"C1: want buffered, got %s\", r.Newly)\n\t}\n\tif r := n.Receive(b1); r.Newly != OutcomeBuffered {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"B1: want buffered, got %s\", r.Newly)\n\t}\n\tr := n.Receive(a1)\n\tif r.Newly != OutcomeDelivered {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"A1: want delivered, got %s\", r.Newly)\n\t}\n\t// Cascade must release B1 then C1, in causal order.\n\tif len(r.Delivered) != 3 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"want 3 deliveries (A1,B1,C1), got %d\", len(r.Delivered))\n\t}\n\tgot := []string{r.Delivered[0].Msg.ID, r.Delivered[1].Msg.ID, r.Delivered[2].Msg.ID}\n\twant := []string{\"A1\", \"B1\", \"C1\"}\n\tfor i := range want {\n\t\tif got[i] != want[i] {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"cascade order = %v, want %v\", got, want)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif n.BufferedCount() != 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"buffer should be empty, has %d\", n.BufferedCount())\n\t}\n\tif n.Clock()[2] != 1 || n.Clock()[0] != 1 || n.Clock()[1] != 1 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"final clock wrong: %v\", n.Clock())\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestDuplicateDeliveredOnce(t *testing.T) {\n\tnames := []string{\"A\", \"B\"}\n\tn := New(1, 2, 10, names)\n\tm := Message{ID: \"A1\", Sender: 0, Seq: 1, Clock: vcOf(2, 0, 1)}\n\n\tif r := n.Receive(m); (\n\t\"testing\"\n\n\t\"causal-broadcast/internal/netlink\"\n)\n\nfunc baseReq(names []string) Request {\n\treturn Request{\n\t\tNames:      names,\n\t\tBufferCap:  1024,\n\t\tSeed:       1,\n\t\tDefaultLink: netlink.Link{BaseDelay: 1.0},\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc deliveredAt(res *Result, node string) []string {\n\tvar out []string\n\tfor _, d := range res.Deliveries {\n\t\tif d.Node == node {\n\t\t\tout = append(out, d.MsgID)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc hasEvent(res *Result, typ, node, msg string) bool {\n\tfor _, e := range res.Trace {\n\t\tif e.Type == typ && e.Node == node && e.MsgID == msg {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\n// Perfect links: every broadcast is delivered everywhere exactly once and\n// causal order verification passes.\nfunc TestPerfectNetworkDeliversAll(t *testing.T) {\n\treq := baseReq([]string{\"A\", \"B\", \"C\"})\n\treq.Broadcasts = []BroadcastSpec{\n\t\t{Time: 0, Sender: 0, Body: \"a1\"},\n\t\t{Time: 1, Sender: 1, Body: \"b1\"},\n\t}\n\tres := New(req).Run()\n\n\tif !res.Complete {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"run should drain completely\")\n\t}\n\tif !res.Diagnostics.CausalOrderOK {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"causal violations: %+v\", res.Diagnostics.Violations)\n\t}\n\tif len(res.Diagnostics.PermanentMissing) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"unexpected missing: %+v\", res.Diagnostics.PermanentMissing)\n\t}\n\t// Each node delivered 2 distinct messages; sender-local delivery counts.\n\tfor _, nf := range res.Nodes {\n\t\tif nf.DeliveredCount != 2 {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"node %s delivered %d, want 2\", nf.Name, nf.DeliveredCount)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// Out-of-order arrival of a causal chain: the successor is held until the\n// predecessor arrives, then released in one cascade.\nfunc TestOutOfOrderChainBuffersAndReleases(t *testing.T) {\n\tnames := []string{\"A\", \"B\", \"C\"}\n\treq := baseReq(names)\n\t// Deterministic links: A->C slow so B1 (which depends on A1 and is sent\n\t// later) overtakes A1 at C.\n\treq.Links = map[[2]int]netlink.Link{\n\t\t{0, 2}: {BaseDelay: 8}, // A -> C slow\n\t\t{1, 2}: {BaseDelay: 1}, // B -> C fast\n\t\t{0, 1}: {BaseDelay: 1},\n\t\t{1, 0}: {BaseDelay: 1},\n\t\t{2, 0}: {BaseDelay: 1},\n\t\t{2, 1}: {BaseDelay: 1},\n\t}\n\treq.Broadcasts = []BroadcastSpec{\n\t\t{Time: 0, Sender: 0, Body: \"a1\"},\n\t\t{Time: 2, Sender: 1, Body: \"b1\"}, // B1 clock = {A:1,B:1}\n\t}\n\tres := New(req).Run()\n\n\tif !hasEvent(res, \"buffered\", \"C\", \"B1\") {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"B1 should have been buffered at C waiting for A1\")\n\t}\n\tif !hasEvent(res, \"deliver\", \"C\", \"A1\") {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"A1 should deliver at C\")\n\t}\n\t// Cascade release trace for B1.\n\tfoundCascade := false\n\tfor _, e := range res.Trace {\n\t\tif e.Type == \"deliver\" && e.Node == \"C\" && e.MsgID == \"B1\" && e.Reason == \"cascade\" {\n\t\t\tfoundCascade = true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif !foundCascade {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"B1 should be released from buffer as a cascade\")\n\t}\n\tgot := deliveredAt(res, \"C\")\n\twant := []string{\"A1\", \"B1\"}\n\tif len(got) != 2 || got[0] != want[0] || got[1] != want[1] {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"C delivery order = %v, want %v\", got, want)\n\t}\n\tif !res.Diagnostics.CausalOrderOK {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"causal violations: %+v\", res.Diagnostics.Violations)\n\t}\n}\n\n// The predecessor is force-dropped at one node: the successor is delivered\n// everywhere else but permanently blocked at that node, and the diagnostics\n// name the lost predecessor as root cause.\nfunc TestPermanentMissingDiagnosis(t *testing.T) {\n\tnames := []string{\"A\", \"B\", \"C\"}\n\treq := baseReq(names)\n\treq.DefaultLink = netlink.Link{BaseDelay: 1}\n\treq.Links = map[[2]int]netlink.Link{\n\t\t{0, 2}: {BaseDelay: 8}, // A -> C slow\n\t\t{1, 2}: {BaseDelay: 1}, // B -> C fast\n\t\t{0, 1}: {BaseDelay: 1},\n\t\t{1, 0}: {BaseDelay: 1},\n\t\t{2, 0}: {BaseDelay: 1},\n\t\t{2, 1}: {BaseDelay: 1},\n\t}\n\treq.DropIDs = map[string][]int{\"A1\": {2}} \"buffered\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"B1 should be buffered at C, state=%s\", rep.State)\n\t}\n\trootWant := \"A1@C\"\n\tfound := false\n\tfor _, r := range rep.RootCauses {\n\t\tif r == rootWant {\n\t\t\tfound = true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif !found {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"root causes = %v, want %s\", rep.RootCauses, rootWant)\n\t}\n\t// B still gets everything.\n\tif got := deliveredAt(res, \"B\"); len(got) != 2 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"B deliveries = %v\", got)\n\t}\n\tif got := deliveredAt(res, \"A\"); len(got) != 2 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"A deliveries = %v\", got)\n\t}\n\tif res.Stats.ForcedDropped == 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"forced drop not counted\")\n\t}\n}\n\n// A message lost outright (no successor) is diagnosed as never-arrived.\nfunc TestNeverArrivedDiagnosis(t *testing.T) {\n\treq := baseReq([]string{\"A\", \"B\"})\n\treq.DefaultLink = netlink.Link{BaseDelay: 1}\n\treq.DropIDs = map[string][]int{\"A1\": {1}}\n\treq.Broadcasts = []BroadcastSpec{{Time: 0, Sender: 0}}\n\tres := New(req).Run()\n\n\tif len(res.Diagnostics.PermanentMissing) != 1 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"want 1 permanent missing, got %+v\", res.Diagnostics.PermanentMissing)\n\t}\n\tm := res.Diagnostics.PermanentMissing[0]\n\tif m.MsgID != \"A1\" || m.Node != \"B\" || m.State != \"never-arrived\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"unexpected report: %+v\", m)\n\t}\n}\n\n// Duplicate packets are a second, late copy of A1 to B.\n\treq.HoldIDs = map[string]map[int][]float64{\n\t\t\"A1\": {1: {5.0}},\n\t}\n\treq.Broadcasts = []BroadcastSpec{{Time: 0, Sender: 0}}\n\tres := New(req).Run()\n\n\tif got := deliveredAt(res, \"B\"); len(got) != 1 || got[0] != \"A1\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"B deliveries = %v, want exactly [A1]\", got)\n\t}\n\tif res.Stats.Duplicates == 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"expected at least one duplicate arrival to be counted\")\n\t}\n}\n\n// Independent concurrent messages must never buffer for one another, even\n// when shuffled by jitter.\nfunc TestConcurrentNoFalseBuffering(t Sender: 0},\n\t\t{Time: 0.2, Sender: 1},\n\t\t{Time: 0.4, Sender: 2},\n\t}\n\tres := New(req).Run()\n\n\tfor _, nf := range res.Nodes {\n\t\tif nf.DeliveredCount != 3 {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"%s delivered e)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif !res.Diagnostics.CausalOrderOK {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"causal violations: %+v\", res.Diagnostics.Violations)\n\t}\n}\n\n// The same seed must reproduce the exact same run.\nfunc TestDeterminism(t *testing.T) {\n\tbuild := func() *Result {\n\t\treq := baseReq([]string{\"A\", \"B\", \"C\"})\n\t\treq.DefaultLink = netlink.Link{\n\t\t\tBaseDelay: 1, Loss: 0.2, Duplicate: 0.2, Jitter: 0.5, ReorderJit: 0.5,\n\t\t}\n\t\tfor i := 0; i < 6; i++ {\n\t\t\treq.Broadcasts = append(req.Broadcasts, BroadcastSpec{Time: float64(i) / 2, Sender: i % 3})\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn New(req).Run()\n\t}\n\tr1 := build()\n\tr2 := build()\n\tif len(r1.Deliveries) != len(r2.Deliveries) || len(r1.Trace) != len(r2.Trace) {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"non-deterministic run lengths\")\n\t}\n\tfor i := range r1.Trace {\n\t\ta, b := r1.Trace[i], r2.Trace[i]\n\t\tif a.Time != b.Time || a.Type != b.Type || a.MsgID != b.MsgID || a.Node != b.Node {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"trace diverges at %d:\\n%+v\\n%+v\", i, a, b)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// Backpressure is observable through the trace when a node's buffer fills.\nfunc TestBackpressureTrace(t *testing.T) {\n\treq := baseReq([]string{\"A\", r < 2; r++ {\n\t\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\t\treq.Broadcasts = append(req.Broadcasts, jsonio.BroadcastJSON{\n\t\t\t\tTime: t,\n\t\t\t\tFrom: names[i],\n\t\t\t\tBody: fmt.Sprintf(\"round-%d-node-%s\", r+1, names[i]),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t\tt += 0.2\n\t\t}\n\t}","originalFile":"// Package scenario builds the built-in demonstration requests: a causal\n// chain (every broadcast depends on the previous one) and a concurrent\n// broadcast burst (independent messages arriving out of order).\npackage scenario\n\nimport (\n\t\"fmt\"\n\n\t\"causal-broadcast/internal/jsonio\"\n)\n\n// Chain builds a causal-chain request.\n//\n// With n nodes, node A broadcasts at time 0; every other node broadcasts\n// once in round-robin order shortly after. The timing makes each broadcast\n// depend causally on the previous one, so out-of-order links force\n// buffering along the chain.\n//\n// If lossLast is true, the penultimate chain message is force-dropped at\n// the final node, so the final message is permanently blocked there and the\n// diagnostics report a root-cause chain.\nfunc Chain(n int, seed int64, lossLast bool) jsonio.Request {\n\tif n < 2 {\n\t\tn = 2\n\t}\n\tnames := nodeNames(n)\n\treq := jsonio.Request{\n\t\tNodes:     names,\n\t\tBufferCap: 1024,\n\t\tNetwork: jsonio.NetworkConfig{\n\t\t\tSeed: ptr(seed),\n\t\t\tDefault: &jsonio.LinkJSON{\n\t\t\t\tBaseDelay:  ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t\tJitter:     ptr(0.9),\n\t\t\t\tReorderJit: ptr(0.6),\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\treq.Broadcasts = append(req.Broadcasts, jsonio.BroadcastJSON{\n\t\t\tTime: float64(i) * 4.0,\n\t\t\tFrom: names[i%n],\n\t\t\tBody: fmt.Sprintf(\"chain-step-%d\", i+1),\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\tif lossLast && n >= 2 {\n\t\tpen := names[n-2]\n\t\tlast := names[n-1]\n\t\treq.Network.DropIDs = append(req.Network.DropIDs, jsonio.DropEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: pen + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDst:   []string{last},\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\treturn req\n}\n\n// Concurrent builds an independent-burst request: every node broadcasts\n// twice in a short window, messages carry no cross-node dependencies. With\n// jittered links they arrive out of order but must all deliver immediately\n// (no causal buffering between independent messages); duplicate copies are\n// suppressed.\nfunc Concurrent(n int, seed int64, duplicate bool) jsonio.Request {\n\tif n < 2 {\n\t\tn = 2\n\t}\n\tnames := nodeNames(n)\n\treq := jsonio.Request{\n\t\tNodes:     names,\n\t\tBufferCap: 1024,\n\t\tNetwork: jsonio.NetworkConfig{\n\t\t\tSeed: ptr(seed),\n\t\t\tDefault: &jsonio.LinkJSON{\n\t\t\t\tBaseDelay:  ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t\tJitter:     ptr(0.95),\n\t\t\t\tReorderJit: ptr(0.9),\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tt := 0.0\n\tfor r := 0; r < 2; r++ {\n\t\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\t\treq.Broadcasts = append(req.Broadcasts, jsonio.BroadcastJSON{\n\t\t\t\tTime: t,\n\t\t\t\tFrom: names[i],\n\t\t\t\tBody: fmt.Sprintf(\"round-%d-node-%s\", r+1, names[i]),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t\tt += 0.2\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif duplicate {\n\t\t// Force an extra late copy of the first broadcast to every node, so\n\t\t// duplicate suppression is always demonstrable regardless of RNG.\n\t\treq.Network.HoldIDs = append(req.Network.HoldIDs, jsonio.HoldEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: names[0] + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDelay: flex(20),\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\treturn req\n}\n\n// flex is a tiny helper to build the flex float list.\nfunc flex(x float64) jsonio.FlexFloat { return jsonio.FlexFloat{x} }\n\nfunc nodeNames(n int) []string {\n\tout := make([]string, n)\n\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\tout[i] = string(rune('A' + i))\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc ptr[T any](v T) *T { return &v }\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":69,"oldLines":10,"newStart":69,"newLines":14,"lines":["     BufferCap: 1024,","     Network: jsonio.NetworkConfig{","       Seed: ptr(seed),","+      // Minimum link delay (base-jitter) is 3 while the whole broadcast","+      // burst ends at ~2n*0.2, so every broadcast happens before any","+      // cross-node delivery: all 2n messages are causally independent,","+      // yet jitter shuffles their arrival order.","       Default: &jsonio.LinkJSON{","-        BaseDelay:  ptr(1.0),","-        Jitter:     ptr(0.95),","-        ReorderJit: ptr(0.9),","+        BaseDelay:  ptr(5.0),","+        Jitter:     ptr(2.0),","+        ReorderJit: ptr(2.0),","       },","     },","   }"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"bd538789-0a92-43b7-9f2c-ef3b9f73577f","session_id":"17e0c499-e52d-4d51-ae66-30adfd094eb4","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp28/a","sessionId":"17e0c499-e52d-4d51-ae66-30adfd094eb4","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp28-a","slug":"twinkly-mixing-kettle"}

until the\n// predecessor arrives, then released in one cascade.\nfunc TestOutOfOrderChainBuffersAndReleases(t *testing.T) {\n\tnames := []string{\"A\", \"B\", \"C\"}\n\treq := baseReq(names)\n\t// 0, Sender: 0, Body: \"a1\"},\n\t\t{Time: 2, Sender: 1, Body: \"b1\"}, // B1 clock = {A:1,B:1}\n\t}\n\tres := New(req).Run()\n\n\tif !hasEvent(res, \"buffered\", \"C\", \"B1\") {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"B1 should have been buffered at C waiting for A1\")\n\t}\n\tif !hasEvent(res, \"deliver\", \"C\", \"A1\") {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"A1 should deliver at C\")\n\t}\n\t// Cascade release trace for B1.\n\tfoundCascade := false\n\tfor _, e := range res.Trace {\n\t\tif e.Type == \"deliver\" && e.Node == \"C\" && e.MsgID == \"B1\" && e.Reason == \"cascade\" {\n\t\t\tfoundCascade = true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif !foundCascade {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"B1 should be released from buffer as a cascade\")\n\t}\n\tgot := deliveredAt(res, \"C\")\n\twant := []string{\"A1\", \"B1\"}\n\tif len(got) != 2 {BaseDelay: 1},\n\t\t{2, 0}: {BaseDelay: 1},\n\t\t{2, 1}: {BaseDelay: 1},\n\t}\n\treq.DropIDs = map[string][]int{\"A1\": {2}} // A1 never reaches C\n\treq.Broadcasts = []BroadcastSpec{\n\t\t{Time: 0, Sender: 0, Body: \"a1\"},\n\t\t{Time: 2, Sender: 1, Body: \"b1\"},\n\t}\n\tres := New(req).Run()\n\n\tvar rep *MissingReport\n\tfor i := range res.Diagnostics.PermanentMissing {\n\t\tif deliveredAt(res, \"A\"); len(got) != 2 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"A deliveries = %v\", got)\n\t}\n\tif res.Stats.ForcedDropped == 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"forced drop not counted\")\n\t}\n}\n\n// A message lost outright (no successor) is diagnosed as never-arrived.\nfunc TestNeverArrivedDiagnosis(t *testing.T) {\n\treq := baseReq([]string{\"A\", \"B\"})\n\treq.DefaultLink = netlink.Link{BaseDelay: err == nil {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"%s: expected validation error\", name)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t})\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestDefaultBufferCap(t *testing.T) {\n\treq := Request{Nodes: []string{\"A\", \"B\"}}\n\tif err := req.Validate(); {"type":"last-prompt","lastPrompt":"从空目录开发“因果广播缓冲”纯后端项目。用Go实现确定性离散事件模拟器与JSON运行接口，节点在单进程内模拟，网络可丢包、重复和乱序，禁止依赖真实集群。实现向量依赖的因果消息投递，未满足依赖先缓冲，重复消息只投递一次，缓冲超额返回背压且不破坏因果顺序。验收：生成链式和并发广播，乱序传递并丢失前驱，验证前驱补齐后释放及永久缺失的诊断。交付源码、README、请求样例与自动化测试；实际运行并如实记录命…","leafUuid":"820b0f31-be62-43cf-9a91-3a12b1f46d81","sessionId":"17e0c499-e52d-4d51-ae66-30adfd094eb4"}

{"type":"last-prompt","lastPrompt":"从空目录开发“因果广播缓冲”纯后端项目。用Go实现确定性离散事件模拟器与JSON运行接口，节点在单进程内模拟，网络可丢包、重复和乱序，禁止依赖真实集群。实现向量依赖的因果消息投递，未满足依赖先缓冲，重复消息只投递一次，缓冲超额返回背压且不破坏因果顺序。验收：生成链式和并发广播，乱序传递并丢失前驱，验证前驱补齐后释放及永久缺失的诊断。交付源码、README、请求样例与自动化测试；实际运行并如实记录命…","leafUuid":"a0f73805-235c-4b8f-94a3-8c4c2ff703c6","sessionId":"17e0c499-e52d-4d51-ae66-30adfd094eb4"}

{"type":"last-prompt","lastPrompt":"从空目录开发“因果广播缓冲”纯后端项目。用Go实现确定性离散事件模拟器与JSON运行接口，节点在单进程内模拟，网络可丢包、重复和乱序，禁止依赖真实集群。实现向量依赖的因果消息投递，未满足依赖先缓冲，重复消息只投递一次，缓冲超额返回背压且不破坏因果顺序。验收：生成链式和并发广播，乱序传递并丢失前驱，验证前驱补齐后释放及永久缺失的诊断。交付源码、README、请求样例与自动化测试；实际运行并如实记录命…","leafUuid":"f672941d-48ef-4f5c-b5d9-e065ccba61e5","sessionId":"17e0c499-e52d-4d51-ae66-30adfd094eb4"}

Links may drop, duplicate and reorder packets, driven by\n// a seeded RNG plus explicit forced rules for reproducible scenarios.\npackage netlink\n\nimport (\n\t\"math/rand\"\n)\n\n// Link are the per-(source,destination) link parameters. Probabilities are\n// in [0,1].\ntype Link struct {\n\tLoss       float64 `json:\"loss\"`\n\tDuplicate  float64 `json:\"duplicate\"`\n\tBaseDelay  float64 `json:\"baseDelay\"`\n\tJitter     float64 `json:\"jitter\"`\n\tReorderJit float64 `json:\"reorderJitter\"`\n}\n\n// Network is the link fabric.\ntype Network struct {\n\tN             int\n\tDefaultLink   Link\n\tLinks         map[[2]int]Link\n\tForcedDrops   map[string][]int // msgID -> destination indices (empty = all)\n\tHolds         map[string]map[int][]float64\n\tRand          *rand.Rand\n}\n\n// New builds a fabric from per-link overrides.\nfunc New(n int, def Link, overrides map[[2]int]Link, seed int64) *Network {\n\tnw := &Network{\n\t\tN:           n,\n\t\tDefaultLink: def,\n\t\tLinks:       make(map[[2]int]Link),\n\t\tForcedDrops: make(map[string][]int),\n\t\tHolds:       make(map[string]map[int][]float64),\n\t\tRand:        rand.New(rand.NewSource(seed)),\n\t}\n\tfor k, v := range overrides {\n\t\tnw.Links[k] = v\n\t}\n\treturn nw\n}\n\n// ForceDrop marks msgID as dropped at dst (-1 = all destinations).\nfunc (nw *Network) ForceDrop(msgID string, dst int) {\n\tnw.ForcedDrops[msgID] = append(nw.ForcedDrops[msgID], dst)\n}\n\n// ForceHold schedules an extra copy of msgID to dst (-1 = all) with the\n// given delay. Multiple ForceHold calls produce multiple delayed copies.\nfunc (nw *Network) ForceHold(msgID string, dst int, delay float64) {\n\tm, ok := nw.Holds[msgID]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\tm = make(map[int][]float64)\n\t\tnw.Holds[msgID] = m\n\t}\n\tif dst == -1 {\n\t\tfor d := 0; d < nw.N; d++ {\n\t\t\tm[d] = append(m[d], delay)\n\t\t}\n\t} else {\n\t\tm[dst] = append(m[dst], delay)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (nw *Network) linkOf(src, dst int) Link {\n\tif l, ok := nw.Links[[2]int{src, dst}]; ok {\n\t\treturn l\n\t}\n\treturn nw.DefaultLink\n}\n\nfunc (nw *Network) forcedDrop(id string, dst int) bool {\n\tfor _, d := range nw.ForcedDrops[id] {\n\t\tif d == -1 || d == dst {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\n// Plan is the outcome of sending one message: zero or more arrival delays,\n// one per surviving packet copy. An empty slice means total loss.\ntype Plan struct {\n\tArrivals []float64\n\t// DropReason is \"\" when delivered, otherwise \"forced\" or \"loss\".\n\tDropReason string\n\t// DupExtra is the number of copies beyond the first one delivered.\n\tDupExtra int\n}\n\n// Send computes what the link (src -> dst) does with m at time now.\n// RNG calls happen in a fixed order (loss, duplicate, delays) so a given\n// seed always produces the same run.\nfunc (nw *Network) Send(mID string, src, dst int, now float64) Plan {\n\tl := nw.linkOf(src, dst)\n\n\tif nw.forcedDrop(mID, dst) {\n\t\treturn Plan{DropReason: \"forced\"}\n\t}\n\tif l.Loss > 0 && nw.Rand.Float64() < l.Loss {\n\t\treturn Plan{DropReason: \"loss\"}\n\t}\n\n\tcopies := 1\n\tif l.Duplicate > 0 && nw.Rand.Float64() < l.Duplicate {\n\t\tcopies++\n\t}\n\tcopies += len(nw.Holds[mID][dst])\n\n\tplan := Plan{}\n\tfor c := 0; c < copies; c++ {\n\t\t// Per-copy uniform jitter around BaseDelay; copies can then pass\n\t\t// each other, which is how reordering appears in a queue-free link\n\t\t// model.\n\t\tdelay := l.BaseDelay + (nw.Rand.Float64()*2-1)*l.Jitter + (nw.Rand.Float64()*2-1)*l.ReorderJit\n\t\tif delay < 0 {\n\t\t\tdelay = 0\n\t\t}\n\t\tplan.Arrivals = append(plan.Arrivals, now+delay)\n\t}\n\t// Scripted extra copies keep their explicit absolute timing.\n\tfor _, d := range nw.Holds[mID][dst] {\n\t\tplan.Arrivals = append(plan.Arrivals, now+d)\n\t}\n\tplan.DupExtra = len(plan.Arrivals) - 1\n\treturn plan\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":20,"oldLines":12,"newStart":20,"newLines":17,"lines":[" "," // Network is the link fabric."," type Network struct {","-  N             int","-  DefaultLink   Link","-  Links         map[[2]int]Link","-  ForcedDrops   map[string][]int // msgID -> destination indices (empty = all)","-  Holds         map[string]map[int][]float64","-  Rand          *rand.Rand","+  N           int","+  DefaultLink Link","+  Links       map[[2]int]Link","+  ForcedDrops map[string][]int // msgID -> destination indices (empty = all)","+  Holds       map[string]map[int][]float64","+  // Delays suppresses the normal link packet for msgID at the listed","+  // destinations and instead emits only the scripted delayed copies. The timing makes each broadcast\n// depend causally on the previous one, so out-of-order links force\n// buffering along the chain.\n//\n// If lossLast is true, the penultimate chain message is force-dropped at\n// the final node, so the final message is permanently blocked there and the\n// diagnostics report a root-cause chain.\nfunc Chain(n int, seed int64, lossLast bool) jsonio.Request {\n\tif n < 2 {\n\t\tn = 2\n\t}\n\tnames := nodeNames(n)\n\treq := jsonio.Request{\n\t\tNodes:     names,\n\t\tBufferCap: 1024,\n\t\tNetwork: jsonio.NetworkConfig{\n\t\t\tSeed: ptr(seed),\n\t\t\tDefault: &jsonio.LinkJSON{\n\t\t\t\tBaseDelay:  ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t\tJitter:     ptr(0.9),\n\t\t\t\tReorderJit: ptr(0.6),\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\treq.Broadcasts = append(req.Broadcasts, jsonio.BroadcastJSON{\n\t\t\tTime: float64(i) * 4.0,\n\t\t\tFrom: names[i%n],\n\t\t\tBody: fmt.Sprintf(\"chain-step-%d\", i+1),\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\tif lossLast && n >= 2 {\n\t\tpen := names[n-2]\n\t\tlast := names[n-1]\n\t\treq.Network.DropIDs = append(req.Network.DropIDs, jsonio.DropEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: pen + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDst:   []string{last},\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\treturn req\n}\n\n// Concurrent builds an independent-burst request: every node broadcasts\n// twice in a short window, messages carry no cross-node dependencies. With\n// jittered links they arrive out of order but must all deliver immediately\n// (no causal buffering between independent messages); duplicate copies are\n// suppressed.\nfunc Concurrent(n int, seed int64, duplicate bool) jsonio.Request {\n\tif n < 2 {\n\t\tn = 2\n\t}\n\tnames := nodeNames(n)\n\treq := jsonio.Request{\n\t\tNodes:     names,\n\t\tBufferCap: 1024,\n\t\tNetwork: jsonio.NetworkConfig{\n\t\t\tSeed: ptr(seed),\n\t\t\t// Minimum link delay (base-jitter) is 2 while the whole burst of\n\t\t\t// 2n broadcasts ends at 2n*0.05 (< 1 for up to ~8 nodes), so\n\t\t\t// every broadcast happens before any cross-node delivery: all\n\t\t\t// messages are causally independent, yet jitter shuffles them.\n\t\t\tDefault: &jsonio.LinkJSON{\n\t\t\t\tBaseDelay:  ptr(3.0),\n\t\t\t\tJitter:     ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t\tReorderJit: ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tt := 0.0\n\tfor r := 0; r < 2; r++ {\n\t\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\t\treq.Broadcasts = append(req.Broadcasts, jsonio.BroadcastJSON{\n\t\t\t\tTime: t,\n\t\t\t\tFrom: names[i],\n\t\t\t\tBody: fmt.Sprintf(\"round-%d-node-%s\", r+1, names[i]),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t\tt += 0.05\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif duplicate {\n\t\t// Force an extra late copy of the first broadcast to every node, so\n\t\t// duplicate suppression is always demonstrable regardless of RNG.\n\t\treq.Network.HoldIDs = append(req.Network.HoldIDs, jsonio.HoldEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: names[0] + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDelay: flex(20),\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\treturn req\n}\n\n// flex is a tiny helper to build the flex float list.\nfunc flex(x float64) jsonio.FlexFloat { return jsonio.FlexFloat{x} }\n\nfunc nodeNames(n int) []string {\n\tout := make([]string, n)\n\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\tout[i] = string(rune('A' + i))\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc ptr[T any](v T) *T { return &v }\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":29,"oldLines":6,"newStart":29,"newLines":8,"lines":["     BufferCap: 1024,","     Network: jsonio.NetworkConfig{","       Seed: ptr(seed),","+      // Steps are 1.5 apart while delays range up to ~2.5, so a","+      // successor can reach a node before its predecessor and be held.","       Default: &jsonio.LinkJSON{","         BaseDelay:  ptr(1.0),","         Jitter:     ptr(0.9),"]},{"oldStart":38,"oldLines":7,"newStart":40,"newLines":7,"lines":["   }","   for i := 0; This is independent of the RNG seed.\n\tfor i := 0; i+2 < n; i++ {\n\t\treq.Network.DelayedIDs = append(req.Network.DelayedIDs, jsonio.HoldEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: names[i] + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDst:   []string{names[i+2]},\n\t\t\tDelay: jsonio.FlexFloat{float64(i)*2.0 + 3.0},\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\tif lossLast && n >= 2 {\n\t\tpen := names[n-2]\n\t\tlast := names[n-1]\n\t\treq.Network.DropIDs = append(req.Network.DropIDs, jsonio.DropEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: pen + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDst:   []string{last},\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\treturn req\n}","originalFile":"// Package scenario builds the built-in demonstration requests: a causal\n// chain (every broadcast depends on the previous one) and a concurrent\n// broadcast burst (independent messages arriving out of order).\npackage scenario\n\nimport (\n\t\"fmt\"\n\n\t\"causal-broadcast/internal/jsonio\"\n)\n\n// Chain builds a causal-chain request.\n//\n// With n nodes, node A broadcasts at time 0; every other node broadcasts\n// once in round-robin order shortly after. The timing makes each broadcast\n// depend causally on the previous one, so out-of-order links force\n// buffering along the chain.\n//\n// If lossLast is true, the penultimate chain message is force-dropped at\n// the final node, so the final message is permanently blocked there and the\n// diagnostics report a root-cause chain.\nfunc Chain(n int, seed int64, lossLast bool) jsonio.Request {\n\tif n < 2 {\n\t\tn = 2\n\t}\n\tnames := nodeNames(n)\n\treq := jsonio.Request{\n\t\tNodes:     names,\n\t\tBufferCap: 1024,\n\t\tNetwork: jsonio.NetworkConfig{\n\t\t\tSeed: ptr(seed),\n\t\t\t// Steps are 1.5 apart while delays range up to ~2.5, so a\n\t\t\t// successor can reach a node before its predecessor and be held.\n\t\t\tDefault: &jsonio.LinkJSON{\n\t\t\t\tBaseDelay:  ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t\tJitter:     ptr(0.9),\n\t\t\t\tReorderJit: ptr(0.6),\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\treq.Broadcasts = append(req.Broadcasts, jsonio.BroadcastJSON{\n\t\t\tTime: float64(i) * 1.5,\n\t\t\tFrom: names[i%n],\n\t\t\tBody: fmt.Sprintf(\"chain-step-%d\", i+1),\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\tif lossLast && n >= 2 {\n\t\tpen := names[n-2]\n\t\tlast := names[n-1]\n\t\treq.Network.DropIDs = append(req.Network.DropIDs, jsonio.DropEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: pen + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDst:   []string{last},\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\treturn req\n}\n\n// Concurrent builds an independent-burst request: every node broadcasts\n// twice in a short window, messages carry no cross-node dependencies. With\n// jittered links they arrive out of order but must all deliver immediately\n// (no causal buffering between independent messages); duplicate copies are\n// suppressed.\nfunc Concurrent(n int, seed int64, duplicate bool) jsonio.Request {\n\tif n < 2 {\n\t\tn = 2\n\t}\n\tnames := nodeNames(n)\n\treq := jsonio.Request{\n\t\tNodes:     names,\n\t\tBufferCap: 1024,\n\t\tNetwork: jsonio.NetworkConfig{\n\t\t\tSeed: ptr(seed),\n\t\t\t// Minimum link delay (base-jitter) is 2 while the whole burst of\n\t\t\t// 2n broadcasts ends at 2n*0.05 (< 1 for up to ~8 nodes), so\n\t\t\t// every broadcast happens before any cross-node delivery: all\n\t\t\t// messages are causally independent, yet jitter shuffles them.\n\t\t\tDefault: &jsonio.LinkJSON{\n\t\t\t\tBaseDelay:  ptr(3.0),\n\t\t\t\tJitter:     ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t\tReorderJit: ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tt := 0.0\n\tfor r := 0; r < 2; r++ {\n\t\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\t\treq.Broadcasts = append(req.Broadcasts, jsonio.BroadcastJSON{\n\t\t\t\tTime: t,\n\t\t\t\tFrom: names[i],\n\t\t\t\tBody: fmt.Sprintf(\"round-%d-node-%s\", r+1, names[i]),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t\tt += 0.05\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif duplicate {\n\t\t// Force an extra late copy of the first broadcast to every node, so\n\t\t// duplicate suppression is always demonstrable regardless of RNG.\n\t\treq.Network.HoldIDs = append(req.Network.HoldIDs, jsonio.HoldEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: names[0] + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDelay: flex(20),\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\treturn req\n}\n\n// flex is a tiny helper to build the flex float list.\nfunc flex(x float64) jsonio.FlexFloat { return jsonio.FlexFloat{x} }\n\nfunc nodeNames(n int) []string {\n\tout := make([]string, n)\n\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\tout[i] = string(rune('A' + i))\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc ptr[T any](v T) *T { return &v }\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":40,"oldLines":11,"newStart":40,"newLines":21,"lines":["   }","   for i := 0; Its own successor\n\t\t// may still arrive there (via normal links) and gets buffered with a\n\t\t// root-cause chain pointing at the dropped predecessor.\n\t\treq.Network.DropIDs = append(req.Network.DropIDs, jsonio.DropEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: pen + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDst:   []string{last},\n\t\t})\n\t\t// Ensure the successor copy reaches the final node even when it is\n\t\t// more than one hop away, so the blocked chain is observable.\n\t\tif prev := n - 3; prev >= 0 {\n\t\t\treq.Network.HoldIDs = append(req.Network.HoldIDs, jsonio.HoldEntry{\n\t\t\t\tMsgID: names[prev] + \"1\",\n\t\t\t\tDst:   []string{last},\n\t\t\t\tDelay: jsonio.FlexFloat{float64(n) * 2.0},\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn req\n}","originalFile":"// Package scenario builds the built-in demonstration requests: a causal\n// chain (every broadcast depends on the previous one) and a concurrent\n// broadcast burst (independent messages arriving out of order).\npackage scenario\n\nimport (\n\t\"fmt\"\n\n\t\"causal-broadcast/internal/jsonio\"\n)\n\n// Chain builds a causal-chain request.\n//\n// With n nodes, node A broadcasts at time 0; every other node broadcasts\n// once in round-robin order shortly after. The timing makes each broadcast\n// depend causally on the previous one, so out-of-order links force\n// buffering along the chain.\n//\n// If lossLast is true, the penultimate chain message is force-dropped at\n// the final node, so the final message is permanently blocked there and the\n// diagnostics report a root-cause chain.\nfunc Chain(n int, seed int64, lossLast bool) jsonio.Request {\n\tif n < 2 {\n\t\tn = 2\n\t}\n\tnames := nodeNames(n)\n\treq := jsonio.Request{\n\t\tNodes:     names,\n\t\tBufferCap: 1024,\n\t\tNetwork: jsonio.NetworkConfig{\n\t\t\tSeed: ptr(seed),\n\t\t\t// Steps are 1.5 apart while delays range up to ~2.5, so a\n\t\t\t// successor can reach a node before its predecessor and be held.\n\t\t\tDefault: &jsonio.LinkJSON{\n\t\t\t\tBaseDelay:  ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t\tJitter:     ptr(0.9),\n\t\t\t\tReorderJit: ptr(0.6),\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\treq.Broadcasts = append(req.Broadcasts, jsonio.BroadcastJSON{\n\t\t\tTime: float64(i) * 2.0,\n\t\t\tFrom: names[i%n],\n\t\t\tBody: fmt.Sprintf(\"chain-step-%d\", i+1),\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\t// Scripted out-of-order delivery: each predecessor message is delayed to\n\t// the node two hops away, so the successor arrives first and is buffered\n\t// until the predecessor catches up. This is independent of the RNG seed.\n\tfor i := 0; i+2 < n; i++ {\n\t\treq.Network.DelayedIDs = append(req.Network.DelayedIDs, jsonio.HoldEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: names[i] + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDst:   []string{names[i+2]},\n\t\t\tDelay: jsonio.FlexFloat{float64(i)*2.0 + 3.0},\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\tif lossLast && n >= 2 {\n\t\tpen := names[n-2]\n\t\tlast := names[n-1]\n\t\treq.Network.DropIDs = append(req.Network.DropIDs, jsonio.DropEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: pen + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDst:   []string{last},\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\treturn req\n}\n\n// Concurrent builds an independent-burst request: every node broadcasts\n// twice in a short window, messages carry no cross-node dependencies. With\n// jittered links they arrive out of order but must all deliver immediately\n// (no causal buffering between independent messages); duplicate copies are\n// suppressed.\nfunc Concurrent(n int, seed int64, duplicate bool) jsonio.Request {\n\tif n < 2 {\n\t\tn = 2\n\t}\n\tnames := nodeNames(n)\n\treq := jsonio.Request{\n\t\tNodes:     names,\n\t\tBufferCap: 1024,\n\t\tNetwork: jsonio.NetworkConfig{\n\t\t\tSeed: ptr(seed),\n\t\t\t// Minimum link delay (base-jitter) is 2 while the whole burst of\n\t\t\t// 2n broadcasts ends at 2n*0.05 (< 1 for up to ~8 nodes), so\n\t\t\t// every broadcast happens before any cross-node delivery: all\n\t\t\t// messages are causally independent, yet jitter shuffles them.\n\t\t\tDefault: &jsonio.LinkJSON{\n\t\t\t\tBaseDelay:  ptr(3.0),\n\t\t\t\tJitter:     ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t\tReorderJit: ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tt := 0.0\n\tfor r := 0; r < 2; r++ {\n\t\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\t\treq.Broadcasts = append(req.Broadcasts, jsonio.BroadcastJSON{\n\t\t\t\tTime: t,\n\t\t\t\tFrom: names[i],\n\t\t\t\tBody: fmt.Sprintf(\"round-%d-node-%s\", r+1, names[i]),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t\tt += 0.05\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif duplicate {\n\t\t// Force an extra late copy of the first broadcast to every node, so\n\t\t// duplicate suppression is always demonstrable regardless of RNG.\n\t\treq.Network.HoldIDs = append(req.Network.HoldIDs, jsonio.HoldEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: names[0] + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDelay: flex(20),\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\treturn req\n}\n\n// flex is a tiny helper to build the flex float list.\nfunc flex(x float64) jsonio.FlexFloat { return jsonio.FlexFloat{x} }\n\nfunc nodeNames(n int) []string {\n\tout := make([]string, n)\n\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\tout[i] = string(rune('A' + i))\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc ptr[T any](v T) *T { return &v }\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":58,"oldLines":10,"newStart":58,"newLines":22,"lines":["   if lossLast && n >= 2 {","     pen := names[n-2]","     last := names[n-1]","+    // Drop the penultimate message at the final node. Its own successor","+    // may still arrive there (via normal links) and gets buffered with a","+    // root-cause chain pointing at the dropped predecessor.","     req.Network.DropIDs = append(req.Network.DropIDs, jsonio.DropEntry{","       MsgID: pen + \"1\",","       Dst:   []string{last},","     })","+    // Ensure the successor copy reaches the final node even when it is","+    // more than one hop away, so the blocked chain is observable.","+    if prev := n - 3; prev >= 0 {","+      req.Network.HoldIDs = append(req.Network.HoldIDs, jsonio.HoldEntry{","+        MsgID: names[prev] + \"1\",","+        Dst:   []string{last},","+        Delay: jsonio.FlexFloat{float64(n) * 2.0},","+      })","+    }","   }","   return req"," }"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"6a092e2b-2f38-4f60-be93-6eea29e48cef","session_id":"17e0c499-e52d-4d51-ae66-30adfd094eb4","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp28/a","sessionId":"17e0c499-e52d-4d51-ae66-30adfd094eb4","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp28-a","slug":"twinkly-mixing-kettle"}

Every later\n\t\t// chain message that reaches the final node is then blocked: B1 is\n\t\t// buffered and its root-cause chain points at A1@<last>; C1/D1 (if\n\t\t// they arrive) are reported as never-arrived with the same root.\n\t\treq.Network.DropIDs = append(req.Network.DropIDs, jsonio.DropEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: names[0] + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDst:   []string{last},\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\treturn req\n}","originalFile":"// Package scenario builds the built-in demonstration requests: a causal\n// chain (every broadcast depends on the previous one) and a concurrent\n// broadcast burst (independent messages arriving out of order).\npackage scenario\n\nimport (\n\t\"fmt\"\n\n\t\"causal-broadcast/internal/jsonio\"\n)\n\n// Chain builds a causal-chain request.\n//\n// With n nodes, node A broadcasts at time 0; every other node broadcasts\n// once in round-robin order shortly after. The timing makes each broadcast\n// depend causally on the previous one, so out-of-order links force\n// buffering along the chain.\n//\n// If lossLast is true, the penultimate chain message is force-dropped at\n// the final node, so the final message is permanently blocked there and the\n// diagnostics report a root-cause chain.\nfunc Chain(n int, seed int64, lossLast bool) jsonio.Request {\n\tif n < 2 {\n\t\tn = 2\n\t}\n\tnames := nodeNames(n)\n\treq := jsonio.Request{\n\t\tNodes:     names,\n\t\tBufferCap: 1024,\n\t\tNetwork: jsonio.NetworkConfig{\n\t\t\tSeed: ptr(seed),\n\t\t\t// Steps are 1.5 apart while delays range up to ~2.5, so a\n\t\t\t// successor can reach a node before its predecessor and be held.\n\t\t\tDefault: &jsonio.LinkJSON{\n\t\t\t\tBaseDelay:  ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t\tJitter:     ptr(0.9),\n\t\t\t\tReorderJit: ptr(0.6),\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\treq.Broadcasts = append(req.Broadcasts, jsonio.BroadcastJSON{\n\t\t\tTime: float64(i) * 2.0,\n\t\t\tFrom: names[i%n],\n\t\t\tBody: fmt.Sprintf(\"chain-step-%d\", i+1),\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\t// Scripted out-of-order delivery: each predecessor message is delayed to\n\t// the node two hops away, so the successor arrives first and is buffered\n\t// until the predecessor catches up. This is independent of the RNG seed.\n\tfor i := 0; i+2 < n; i++ {\n\t\treq.Network.DelayedIDs = append(req.Network.DelayedIDs, jsonio.HoldEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: names[i] + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDst:   []string{names[i+2]},\n\t\t\tDelay: jsonio.FlexFloat{float64(i)*2.0 + 3.0},\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\tif lossLast && n >= 2 {\n\t\tpen := names[n-2]\n\t\tlast := names[n-1]\n\t\t// Drop the penultimate message at the final node. Its own successor\n\t\t// may still arrive there (via normal links) and gets buffered with a\n\t\t// root-cause chain pointing at the dropped predecessor.\n\t\treq.Network.DropIDs = append(req.Network.DropIDs, jsonio.DropEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: pen + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDst:   []string{last},\n\t\t})\n\t\t// Ensure the successor copy reaches the final node even when it is\n\t\t// more than one hop away, so the blocked chain is observable.\n\t\tif prev := n - 3; prev >= 0 {\n\t\t\treq.Network.HoldIDs = append(req.Network.HoldIDs, jsonio.HoldEntry{\n\t\t\t\tMsgID: names[prev] + \"1\",\n\t\t\t\tDst:   []string{last},\n\t\t\t\tDelay: jsonio.FlexFloat{float64(n) * 2.0},\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn req\n}\n\n// Concurrent builds an independent-burst request: every node broadcasts\n// twice in a short window, messages carry no cross-node dependencies. With\n// jittered links they arrive out of order but must all deliver immediately\n// (no causal buffering between independent messages); duplicate copies are\n// suppressed.\nfunc Concurrent(n int, seed int64, duplicate bool) jsonio.Request {\n\tif n < 2 {\n\t\tn = 2\n\t}\n\tnames := nodeNames(n)\n\treq := jsonio.Request{\n\t\tNodes:     names,\n\t\tBufferCap: 1024,\n\t\tNetwork: jsonio.NetworkConfig{\n\t\t\tSeed: ptr(seed),\n\t\t\t// Minimum link delay (base-jitter) is 2 while the whole burst of\n\t\t\t// 2n broadcasts ends at 2n*0.05 (< 1 for up to ~8 nodes), so\n\t\t\t// every broadcast happens before any cross-node delivery: all\n\t\t\t// messages are causally independent, yet jitter shuffles them.\n\t\t\tDefault: &jsonio.LinkJSON{\n\t\t\t\tBaseDelay:  ptr(3.0),\n\t\t\t\tJitter:     ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t\tReorderJit: ptr(1.0),\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tt := 0.0\n\tfor r := 0; r < 2; r++ {\n\t\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\t\treq.Broadcasts = append(req.Broadcasts, jsonio.BroadcastJSON{\n\t\t\t\tTime: t,\n\t\t\t\tFrom: names[i],\n\t\t\t\tBody: fmt.Sprintf(\"round-%d-node-%s\", r+1, names[i]),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t\tt += 0.05\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif duplicate {\n\t\t// Force an extra late copy of the first broadcast to every node, so\n\t\t// duplicate suppression is always demonstrable regardless of RNG.\n\t\treq.Network.HoldIDs = append(req.Network.HoldIDs, jsonio.HoldEntry{\n\t\t\tMsgID: names[0] + \"1\",\n\t\t\tDelay: flex(20),\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\treturn req\n}\n\n// flex is a tiny helper to build the flex float list.\nfunc flex(x float64) jsonio.FlexFloat { return jsonio.FlexFloat{x} }\n\nfunc nodeNames(n int) []string {\n\tout := make([]string, n)\n\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\tout[i] = string(rune('A' + i))\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc ptr[T any](v T) *T { return &v }\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":56,"oldLines":24,"newStart":56,"newLines":15,"lines":["     })","   }","   if lossLast && n >= 2 {","-    pen := names[n-2]","     last := names[n-1]","-    // Drop the penultimate message at the final node. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"4cbf6df9-1b01-4ebc-a61e-fe131829c24a","timestamp":"2026-09-23T05:56:10.601Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp28/a/internal/netlink/network.go","oldString":"// Send computes what the link (src -> dst) does with m at time now.\n// RNG calls happen in a fixed order (loss, duplicate, delays) so a given\n// seed always produces the same run.\nfunc (nw *Network) Send(mID string, src, dst int, now float64) Plan {\n\t// Scripted late arrivals replace the normal packet entirely.\n\tif delays, ok := nw.Delays[mID][dst]; ok && len(delays) > 0 {\n\t\tarr := make([]float64, len(delays))\n\t\tfor i, d := range delays {\n\t\t\tarr[i] = now + d\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn Plan{Arrivals: arr}\n\t}\n\n\tl := nw.linkOf(src, dst)\n\n\tif nw.forcedDrop(mID, dst) {\n\t\treturn Plan{DropReason: \"forced\"}\n\t}\n\tif l.Loss > 0 && nw.Rand.Float64() < l.Loss {\n\t\treturn Plan{DropReason: \"loss\"}\n\t}","newString":"// Send computes what the link (src -> dst) does with m at time now.\n// RNG calls happen in a fixed order (loss, duplicate, delays) so a given\n// seed always produces the same run.\nfunc (nw *Network) Send(mID string, src, dst int, now float64) Plan {\n\tl := nw.linkOf(src, dst)\n\n\tif nw.forcedDrop(mID, dst) {\n\t\treturn Plan{DropReason: \"forced\"}\n\t}\n\n\t// Scripted late arrivals replace the normal packet entirely.\n\tif delays, ok := nw.Delays[mID][dst]; ok && len(delays) > 0 {\n\t\tarr := make([]float64, len(delays))\n\t\tfor i, d := range delays {\n\t\t\tarr[i] = now + d\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn Plan{Arrivals: arr}\n\t}\n\n\tif l.Loss > 0 && nw.Rand.Float64() < l.Loss {\n\t\treturn Plan{DropReason: \"loss\"}\n\t}","originalFile":"// Package netlink models the unreliable links between simulated nodes.\n// It never performs real I/O: sending a message only schedules simulated\n// arrival events. Links may drop, duplicate and reorder packets, driven by\n// a seeded RNG plus explicit forced rules for reproducible scenarios.\npackage netlink\n\nimport (\n\t\"math/rand\"\n)\n\n// Link are the per-(source,destination) link parameters. Probabilities are\n// in [0,1].\ntype Link struct {\n\tLoss       float64 `json:\"loss\"`\n\tDuplicate  float64 `json:\"duplicate\"`\n\tBaseDelay  float64 `json:\"baseDelay\"`\n\tJitter     float64 `json:\"jitter\"`\n\tReorderJit float64 `json:\"reorderJitter\"`\n}\n\n// Network is the link fabric.\ntype Network struct {\n\tN           int\n\tDefaultLink Link\n\tLinks       map[[2]int]Link\n\tForcedDrops map[string][]int // msgID -> destination indices (empty = all)\n\tHolds       map[string]map[int][]float64\n\t// Delays suppresses the normal link packet for msgID at the listed\n\t// destinations and instead emits only the scripted delayed copies. This\n\t// models a retransmission that arrives much later (used to script\n\t// buffering/backpressure deterministically).\n\tDelays map[string]map[int][]float64\n\tRand   *rand.Rand\n}\n\n// New builds a fabric from per-link overrides.\nfunc New(n int, def Link, overrides map[[2]int]Link, seed int64) *Network {\n\tnw := &Network{\n\t\tN:           n,\n\t\tDefaultLink: def,\n\t\tLinks:       make(map[[2]int]Link),\n\t\tForcedDrops: make(map[string][]int),\n\t\tHolds:       make(map[string]map[int][]float64),\n\t\tDelays:      make(map[string]map[int][]float64),\n\t\tRand:        rand.New(rand.NewSource(seed)),\n\t}\n\tfor k, v := range overrides {\n\t\tnw.Links[k] = v\n\t}\n\treturn nw\n}\n\n// ForceDrop marks msgID as dropped at dst (-1 = all destinations).\nfunc (nw *Network) ForceDrop(msgID string, dst int) {\n\tnw.ForcedDrops[msgID] = append(nw.ForcedDrops[msgID], dst)\n}\n\n// ForceHold schedules an extra copy of msgID to dst (-1 = all) with the\n// given delay. Multiple ForceHold calls produce multiple delayed copies.\nfunc (nw *Network) ForceHold(msgID string, dst int, delay float64) {\n\tm, ok := nw.Holds[msgID]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\tm = make(map[int][]float64)\n\t\tnw.Holds[msgID] = m\n\t}\n\tif dst == -1 {\n\t\tfor d := 0; d < nw.N; d++ {\n\t\t\tm[d] = append(m[d], delay)\n\t\t}\n\t} else {\n\t\tm[dst] = append(m[dst], delay)\n\t}\n}\n\n// ForceDelay suppresses the normal packet of msgID to dst and emits only\n// scripted delayed copies (a deterministic late arrival / retransmission).\nfunc (nw *Network) ForceDelay(msgID string, dst int, delays ...float64) {\n\tm, ok := nw.Delays[msgID]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\tm = make(map[int][]float64)\n\t\tnw.Delays[msgID] = m\n\t}\n\tm[dst] = append(m[dst], delays...)\n}\n\nfunc (nw *Network) linkOf(src, dst int) Link {\n\tif l, ok := nw.Links[[2]int{src, dst}]; ok {\n\t\treturn l\n\t}\n\treturn nw.DefaultLink\n}\n\nfunc (nw *Network) forcedDrop(id string, dst int) bool {\n\tfor _, d := range nw.ForcedDrops[id] {\n\t\tif d == -1 || d == dst {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\n// Plan is the outcome of sending one message: zero or more arrival delays,\n// one per surviving packet copy. An empty slice means total loss.\ntype Plan struct {\n\tArrivals []float64\n\t// DropReason is \"\" when delivered, otherwise \"forced\" or \"loss\".\n\tDropReason string\n\t// DupExtra is the number of copies beyond the first one delivered.\n\tDupExtra int\n}\n\n// Send computes what the link (src -> dst) does with m at time now.\n// RNG calls happen in a fixed order (loss, duplicate, delays) so a given\n// seed always produces the same run.\nfunc (nw *Network) Send(mID string, src, dst int, now float64) Plan {\n\t// Scripted late arrivals replace the normal packet entirely.\n\tif delays, ok := nw.Delays[mID][dst]; ok && len(delays) > 0 {\n\t\tarr := make([]float64, len(delays))\n\t\tfor i, d := range delays {\n\t\t\tarr[i] = now + d\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn Plan{Arrivals: arr}\n\t}\n\n\tl := nw.linkOf(src, dst)\n\n\tif nw.forcedDrop(mID, dst) {\n\t\treturn Plan{DropReason: \"forced\"}\n\t}\n\tif l.Loss > 0 && nw.Rand.Float64() < l.Loss {\n\t\treturn Plan{DropReason: \"loss\"}\n\t}\n\n\tcopies := 1\n\tif l.Duplicate > 0 && nw.Rand.Float64() < l.Duplicate {\n\t\tcopies++\n\t}\n\tcopies += len(nw.Holds[mID][dst])\n\n\tplan := Plan{}\n\tfor c := 0; c < copies; c++ {\n\t\t// Per-copy uniform jitter around BaseDelay; copies can then pass\n\t\t// each other, which is how reordering appears in a queue-free link\n\t\t// model.\n\t\tdelay := l.BaseDelay + (nw.Rand.Float64()*2-1)*l.Jitter + (nw.Rand.Float64()*2-1)*l.ReorderJit\n\t\tif delay < 0 {\n\t\t\tdelay = 0\n\t\t}\n\t\tplan.Arrivals = append(plan.Arrivals, now+delay)\n\t}\n\t// Scripted extra copies keep their explicit absolute timing.\n\tfor _, d := range nw.Holds[mID][dst] {\n\t\tplan.Arrivals = append(plan.Arrivals, now+d)\n\t}\n\tplan.DupExtra = len(plan.Arrivals) - 1\n\treturn plan\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":113,"oldLines":6,"newStart":113,"newLines":12,"lines":[" // RNG calls happen in a fixed order (loss, duplicate, delays) so a given"," // seed always produces the same run."," func (nw *Network) Send(mID string, src, dst int, now float64) Plan {","+  l := nw.linkOf(src, dst)","+","+  if nw.forcedDrop(mID, dst) {","+    return Plan{DropReason: \"forced\"}","+  }","+","   // Scripted late arrivals replace the normal packet entirely.","   if delays, ok := nw.Delays[mID][dst];
